= CHERIoT memory subsystem: FPV testbench architecture
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures

This doc is the high-level view of how the CHERIoT memory subsystem (`cheriot_mem_sys`) is
verified with formal property verification (FPV): the three checkers it is split into, how they
share one FPV environment, the contracts that link them, the order of the proofs, and the
end-to-end requirements closed by combining their results. Each checker's boundary, environment,
models and checks are in its microarchitecture (uarch) doc; how the design works is in the
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc[design architecture]; the testpoints are in
the testplans.

== Overview

=== FPV terms used here

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning here

|Free input |an input the tool may set to anything, in any cycle
|Assumption |a rule that limits a free input to what the real neighbour does; each one cites the
spec or a contract, because a wrong assumption hides real bugs
|Assertion, cover |an assertion is a property the design must meet, from a testplan check; a cover
is a scenario the tool must show is reachable, or the assertions about it prove nothing
|Checker |one part of the testbench: the real RTL it holds, its rules on its neighbours and its
properties
|Cut point |one signal made a free input; the logic that drives it is ignored
|Contract |a property proven in one checker and assumed in another, so a small checker can rely on
a neighbour without holding it
|Composition |closing a requirement by combining proven results of several checkers
|===

'''

[[checkers]]
=== Three checkers

*Rule:* each checker holds the real RTL of one part of the subsystem. Where two checkers meet, a
contract is proven on one side and assumed on the other, and no proof assumes a contract proven with
its own help (<<contracts>>). A proof of the whole subsystem at once may never finish; small
checkers do, and the contracts link them so nothing falls in between.

.The three checkers over the real subsystem, and the contracts (Cn, <<contracts>>) where they meet
image::cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch_figures.svg#fig1[Three checkers,align=center,width=820,height=781]

[cols="2,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Real RTL, checked there |Testpoints, and how they are checked

|[[tag_path]]1 Tag path
|the core's tag filter with its WTRC (write-to-read-and-compare filter), the 2:1 tag arbiter, the
tag clear squash, the RMW (read-modify-write) filter, the alert logic
|checker 1 testplan; xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc[checker 1 uarch]

|[[meta_access]]2 Meta access
|the four access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter onto the meta SRAM port `meta_sram_tl`
|checker 2 testplan; checker 2 uarch

|[[revocation_checker]]3 Revocation
|the TBRE (background revocation engine) with its mover, TRVK (tag revocation) filter and tag
filter; its sweep control and interrupt; the core write tracker; the tag clear squash and the 2:1
tag arbiter again; the alert logic
|checker 3 testplan; xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_revocation_uarch.adoc[checker 3 uarch]

|Register-file unit
|the register file
|the csr testpoint; <<reg_file_unit>>
|===

* The split into these three checkers is in force. The 2:1 tag arbiter sits between
  the tag filters and the RMW filter, so it is in checker 1. Checker 3 keeps it as
  real RTL too: turning a stale clear into a read, and holding a clear at the RMW filter, are
  revocation behaviour ([ToO] Revocation Engine).
* *Each checker checks the transactions on its boundary ports; none builds a memory.* What the meta
  SRAM or `xbar_main` does with a correct transaction is that memory's own verification.
* Every checker, the same way: reset is free mid-run; the mode input
  `cheriot_ena_i` takes any value, stable from reset; no assumption limits data, so
  a meta word or a capability can hold any value; a broken bus integrity is legal stimulus.
* Cut points only add behaviours: every proof holds for the real design. A CEX (counterexample)
  that needs a removed block to do what the real block cannot is an abstraction artefact.
* No parameter reduction: the instance parameters are already small (2 outstanding, 32-bit words).
* The waveform view of every checker's state: the
  debug view uarch.

'''

[[build]]
=== How the checkers are built

*Rule:* every checker binds to `cheriot_mem_sys` with the Earl Grey parameters. They differ only in
which instances they remove.

[cols="3,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Block |1 Tag path |2 Meta access |3 Revocation

|core's tag filter, with WTRC |checked |cut |cut (contracts C6, C7)
|2:1 tag arbiter |checked |cut |kept
|tag clear squash, core write tracker |kept |not used |checked
|RMW filter |checked |cut (contract C4) |cut (contract C2)
|four access checkers |cut (contract C1) |checked |cut (contract C1)
|4:1 arbiter |cut |checked |cut
|TBRE: mover, TRVK filter, tag filter |cut (contracts C3a, C3b, C11, C21, C22) |cut (contract C5) |checked
|sweep control: start, status, epoch, interrupt |not used |not used |checked
|register file |cut |cut |cut; its outputs follow the register file model (contract C20)
|alert logic |checked: tag path faults |not used |checked: engine faults
|===

* *Checked*: real RTL with testplan checks on it. *Kept*: real RTL the checks rely on. *Cut*:
  removed, its outputs free, bound by the contract named. *Not used*: no property depends on it;
  the tool drops it from the proof.
* Why one top for all three: the glue between the blocks (the tag clear squash, the core write
  tracker, the sweep control, the alert inputs) is logic in `cheriot_mem_sys.sv` itself, so a
  hand-built wrapper would rebuild it; and the real ports are the ones watched.
* How a block is removed: the design is elaborated whole, and each checker's task puts a cut point
  on every output of each instance it removes. Nothing is blackboxed by module name, so checker 3
  can keep the engine's tag filter while it removes the core's instance of the same module.

[[shared_top]]
==== One environment, one task per checker, another only where a check needs a different setup

*Rule:* one FPV top holds the design, with one checker module bound into it that holds every
checker. Each checker holds its own rules on its neighbours, written with the macro `ENV_RULE`: an
assumption in a formal build, an assertion in a simulation build, so the same rules check the real
neighbours' traffic there. The design is analyzed and elaborated once. Each checker has one Jasper
task, `task_<Checker>_Main`, and gets another only where a check cannot share its setup:

* the check needs a safety assumption that would narrow the main task's checks, or leave their
  covers unreachable;
* the check needs an assumption dropped that the main task's checks rest on;
* proving it in the main task would close an assume-guarantee cycle: two contracts, each proven
  while assuming the other.

An assumption that only says "eventually" is no reason: Jasper does not use it on a safety check
([Jasper] p.990, `get_needed_assumptions -include_liveness_assumes`).

.The one FPV environment: the checker module bound into the whole design
image::cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch_figures.svg#fig2[One FPV environment,align=center,width=820,height=498]

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Part |What it is

|FPV top |`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env`: `cheriot_mem_sys` with every input free
|Checker module |`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_checker`, bound by `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_checker_bind`: every
port of `cheriot_mem_sys` and the internal nets the checkers watch; it holds each checker
|Tasks |`task_`, the checker in CamelCase (`TagPath`, `MetaAccess`, `Revocation`, `RegFile`), then
`Main` or what sets the task apart. Each uarch lists its checker's tasks
|Design asserts |the RTL's own `ASSERT` macros inside a checker are copied into its tasks as
targets, never as assumptions; each task file's `dut_asserts` procedure lists them
|Liveness |the liveness checks and the fairness assumptions sit under `FPV_ON` only: a simulation
ends, so an "eventually" still open at its end proves nothing
|===

* *One script*, the Jasper check script, kept outside this repository: it analyzes and
  elaborates once, then makes each checker's tasks from its task file. A task copies its own
  assumptions by label, never every assumption.

'''

[[abvip_placement]]
==== Where each bus checker sits: with the bus it watches

*Rule:* a bus that crosses the edge of the subsystem gets its TL-UL protocol checker (ABVIP,
assertion-based verification IP) in the shared checker module. A link between two blocks inside
the design gets its protocol checker in the checker that owns that link.

* The seven edge buses belong to no single checker: the core's data port, the subsystem's host
  port and the engine's host port to `xbar_main`, the core's bitmap port, the bitmap window, the
  meta SRAM port and the register bus. One copy each serves every checker and the
  subsystem-level proof (<<subsystem_proof>>).
* An ABVIP on a port the testbench plays takes that end's role in formal (`PlayHost`,
  `PlayDevice`); on a link with both ends real, and in simulation, it checks both ends
  (`CheckBoth`).
* An ABVIP holds TL-UL's own rules only. A rule specific to this design (which addresses hold
  capabilities, the order of a capability's two halves) is an assumption in the checker that needs
  it, on top of the ABVIP.

'''

[[reg_file_unit]]
==== The register-file unit: contract C20 on the real register file

*Rule:* contract C20 is proven on the real register file (`u_reg_regs`) with everything else cut,
so the hardware side (`hw2reg`) is free and the contract holds for every engine behaviour. The
generic CSR tests cannot prove it: they never start a sweep (`TBRE_START` is excluded from them
and the simulation testbench runs with CHERIoT mode off), so they never see `TBRE_REGWEN`
lowered by hardware.

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Part |Holds

|Boundary |`regs_tl_d` (the TL-UL ABVIP plays the host), `reg2hw` (to the hardware) and `hw2reg` (from it); the sweep-control glue in `cheriot_mem_sys.sv` stays real, so `TBRE_REGWEN` follows a taken start

|Model |the value `TBRE_STATUS.busy` holds (the hardware's last write), and the data a good read of `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS`, `TBRE_REGWEN` or `TBRE_STATUS.busy` must return

|Checks |the csr checks the generic CSR tests cannot reach: the lock, the sweep registers kept, `INTR_STATE` set and cleared, the request rate; and contract C20: the start strobe, `INTR_STATE` rising, the read side of `TBRE_STATUS.busy`

|Rules |the ABVIP's host rules only; no rule on `hw2reg`

|Files |`fpv/reg_file/rfchk_checker.sv` and its task file `task_RegFile_Main`; instantiated in the one checker as `u_rfchk_checker`
|===

A good request is a whole aligned word with valid command and data integrity; any other request
may be answered with `d_error`, and the checks claim nothing for its data. The sticky error bits
`start_err` and `sweep_err` stay with the generic CSR tests: when software clears one in the
cycle the hardware sets it, software's clear wins (DV reading, question an open question), so
that cycle is covered here, not asserted.

== Contracts and composition

[[contracts]]
=== Contracts

*Rule:* a contract is proven where its logic is and assumed where it is needed. Each is checked by
the testplan check linked in its row (contracts testpoint).

[cols="1,6,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Contract |Proven in |Assumed in

|C1 |On each access checker's requester port, every request is accepted and answered, given the
meta SRAM answers and every requester takes its answers
(CHK_CONTRACTS_01) |2, liveness |1 and 3, liveness
|C2 |On the RMW filter's upstream port, every request is accepted and answered, given contract C1
(CHK_CONTRACTS_02) |1, liveness |3, liveness
|C3a |On the engine's tag filter's meta port, a request, its tag and its bit select stay unchanged
until accepted (CHK_CONTRACTS_03); and the engine's clear report stays
unchanged while its clear waits at the RMW filter |3, safety |1, safety
|C3b |The engine's tag filter takes every meta answer in the cycle it is offered
(CHK_CONTRACTS_04) |3, safety |1, liveness
|C4 |On the RMW filter's downstream port, every answer offered is taken
(CHK_CONTRACTS_05) |1, liveness |2, liveness
|C5 |On the engine's bitmap port, every answer offered is taken
(CHK_CONTRACTS_06) |3, liveness |2, liveness
|C6 |The core's tag filter answers the core's requests in request order
(CHK_CONTRACTS_07) |1, safety |3, safety
|C7 |On the core's tag filter's meta port, a request, its tag and its bit select stay unchanged
until accepted (CHK_CONTRACTS_08) |1, safety |3, safety
|C8 |The RMW filter and the WTRC raise their fault inputs to the alert only for their listed causes
(CHK_CONTRACTS_09) |1, safety |none: used by composition
|C9 |The engine and the register file raise their fault inputs only for their listed causes
(CHK_CONTRACTS_10) |3 (engine), CSR tests (register file) |1, safety
|C10 |On the RMW filter's downstream port, the tag access checker answers a cycle or more after the
request, in order, held until taken (CHK_CONTRACTS_11) |2, safety,
given assumption A16 |1, safety
|C11 |The engine's tag filter addresses whole meta words
(CHK_CONTRACTS_12) |3, safety |1, safety
|C20 |The register file's outputs to the engine follow the register file model: sweep range locked
while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 0, start strobe only while it is 1, interrupt state rising only on a set
request, `TBRE_STATUS.busy` as the engine wrote it (csr) |register-file unit
|3, every run
|C21 |The engine's tag filter's meta port follows the TL-UL rules, and each request is a whole-word
`Get` or `PutFullData` (CHK_CONTRACTS_13) |3, safety |1, every run
|C22 |The engine's tag filter leaves bit 7 of `a_source` clear; no testplan check yet |3, safety
|1, every run
|C12, C13 |Proposed: the RMW filter's and the engine's requests to the access checkers follow the
TL-UL host rules, with the top two `a_source` bits 0 (checker 2 uarch) |1 and 3
|2, every run
|===

* Contracts C12 and C13 close two cycles with contract C10: C10 needs C12, which checker 1 proves
  assuming C10; the engine's bitmap port the same with C13. Until decision D32 breaks them, every
  checker 2 result is conditional on them.
* The other contracts form no cycle: C3a, C3b, C5, C10, C11, C21 and C22 need no contract; C20
  comes from the register-file unit; C6 and C7 need C3a; C4 needs C3b; C1 needs C4 and C5; C2
  needs C1 and C3b. A proof that turns out to need a contract not listed here stops the order.
* The core's tag filter holds its meta requests (contract C7) only if the core holds its requests
  until accepted (assumption A1, question an open question). The fault-cause contracts C8 and C9
  wait on decision D15.

[[proof_order]]
=== Proof order

*Rule:* a run starts only when every contract it assumes has been proven by an earlier run. Covers
run first in every run, and a result counts as proven only once every contract it assumes is
proven.

[cols="1,3,3,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Stage |Run |Jasper task |Proves |Assumes

|1 |2 Meta access, safety |`task_MetaAccess_Main` |its safety checks |C12, C13 (proposed)
|1 |2 Meta access, contract C10 |`task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder` |C10 |assumption A16; C12
|1 |Register file |`task_RegFile_Main` |C20; the `csr` checks the CSR tests cannot reach |nothing
|1 |3 Revocation, safety A |checker 3's task |C3a, C3b, C11, C21, C22 |C20
|1 |3 Revocation, liveness A |checker 3's task |C5 |C20
|2 |1 Tag path, safety |`task_TagPath_Main` |every safety check of checker 1, the alert checks;
C6, C7 |C3a, C10, C11, C21, C22
|2 |1 Tag path, liveness A |`task_TagPath_TagsRspTaken` |C4 |C3a, C3b, C10, C11, C21, C22
|3 |3 Revocation, safety B |checker 3's task |the engine's safety checks |C6, C7, C20
|3 |2 Meta access, liveness A |`task_MetaAccess_Main` |`meta_flow` _request eventually accepted_
|C12, C13
|3 |2 Meta access, liveness B |`task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder` |C1; `meta_flow` _request
eventually answered_ |C4, C5, C12, C13
|4 |1 Tag path, liveness B |`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered` |C2; checker 1's liveness checks |C1,
C3a, C3b, C10, C11, C21, C22
|5 |3 Revocation, liveness B |checker 3's task |`tbre_done`: every sweep ends |C1, C2, C20
|===

* A task may hold runs of two stages. `task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder` proves contract C10 at
  stage 1 although it also assumes C4 and C5, proven at stage 2: those are "eventually" rules,
  which Jasper does not use on C10's safety checks ([Jasper] p.990).
* The check script enforces the order with a gate between stages: it reads the proof status of
  each contract the next task needs, converts the proven ones into assumptions of that task, and
  stops if any is not proven (a time-out counts as not proven). The stage order is written in the
  script; a contract proven under a premise (C10 under assumption A16) carries the premise; the
  status counts in one Jasper session only; each conversion names its assertions in a list, never
  by a name glob.

'''

[[composition]]
=== End-to-end requirements by composition

*Rule:* an end-to-end requirement no single checker holds is closed by combining proven checks of
the checkers with stated premises. No memory is modelled. The testpoints, with the checks each
requirement follows from, are in the subsystem testplan:
tag_read_after_write,
tag_no_deadlock and rev_end_to_end.

The argument for the tag path: checker 1 proves the tag filter asks for the right word and bit,
the arbiter passes each request on and returns each answer to the filter that asked, and the RMW
filter reads and writes only that bit, one operation at a time. Checker 2 proves the tag port
passes those requests to `meta_sram_tl` unchanged and no other port reaches the tag words. If the
meta SRAM keeps what it is given (premise P1), the tag read back is the one last written. Each
chain runs port to port with no unchecked block in between.

[cols="1,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Premise |Who verifies it

|P1 |The meta SRAM returns, for a read, the word last written to that address (assumption A11).
|the meta SRAM controller (`sram_ctrl`) verification; [IF] `meta_sram_tl`: "Host TL-UL port to the
external meta SRAM controller's RAM interface"
|P2 |No `Get` of a tag write has been answered with no `d_error` and a broken integrity since
reset (question an open question); from that answer on only the latched alert is claimed, and the
alert sender, a fatal alert, keeps signalling until reset. |the alert sender: OpenTitan's own FPV of
the alert sender and receiver (`hw/ip/prim/fpv/tb/prim_alert_rxtx_fatal_tb.sv`), if option (a) of
decision D12 holds
|===

A composed requirement is closed once every check it follows from is proven and the argument is
agreed in review.

'''

[[subsystem_proof]]
=== Subsystem-level proof

*Rule:* once the three checkers prove on their own, one more task proves them together on the
whole subsystem, with no cut and no contract assumed. Sign-off rests on the checker tasks and the
gated contracts; the subsystem task shows the contracts and the internal rules were the right ones.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|In the subsystem task |What it is

|Targets |every assertion of the three checkers and the register-file unit, contracts included
|Assumptions |the rules on the external ports only: the core, `xbar_main`, the meta SRAM, the
register bus and the alert receiver
|Not copied |every rule on an internal neighbour: the real block is present, so the rule is a fact
there, and a false one shows as a CEX on the check that relied on it
|ABVIPs on internal ports |`CheckBoth`, as in simulation
|Cuts |none
|===

The engine's sweep and the capability count make the state space deep, so the task runs bounded
first, its depth recorded with the run. It needs every checker built, so it is the milestone after
the three checkers prove.

'''

=== Convergence

. A checker that does not converge is handled in this order: split the obligation, then cut points,
  then symbolic tracking, then helper invariants, then a bounded result with its bound.
. Ready splits: checker 1 into the tag filter alone, and the arbiter with the RMW filter, with
  contracts on the tag filter's meta port; checker 3 into the sweep control with the mover cut, and
  the mover with the TRVK filter, with a contract on the mover's start interface.
. `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` and the epoch count stay full width; a counter abstraction is added only if a
  proof needs it, and recorded in the ledger.

[[decisions_made]]
=== Decisions in force

*Rule:* every decision of this doc that shapes the testbench today. The uarchs number their
decisions after them. Closed decisions: git log.

[cols="5,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Decision |Why |What it means for the results

|The subsystem is split into three checkers. |Small checkers converge; contracts link
them (<<checkers>>). |Every end-to-end requirement no single checker holds is closed by composition
(<<composition>>).
|In checker 3 the register file is cut, its outputs following the register file model (contract
C20); the register rows are checked by the register-file unit and the generic CSR tests (decision). |The registers are tested on their own; a smaller checker 3. |Checker 3 does not check,
through `regs_tl_d`, the lock or that a read right after a start sees the sweep; the
register-file unit and the CSR tests do.
|The bus integrity code is out of scope: the testbench calls `tlul_pkg`{empty}'s integrity
functions as the interface definition (question an open question;
xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc#integrity_code[checker 1 uarch, integrity code]).
From RTL packages the testbench also keeps interface types and widths, the multi-bit mode
constants and the register offsets. |The code is a shared OpenTitan primitive that both ends of
every link use, with its own formal testbench (`hw/ip/prim/fpv`). |Every subsystem bug stays
visible: wrong fields encoded, old integrity forwarded, a broken code missed. Left to OpenTitan: a
bug inside those functions.
|No run variant breaks the core's own access order. |A core that breaks it is out of
scope: what the design does then is undetermined. |Those cases are marked out of scope in the
testplan (Not covered by this testplan), not left vacuous.
|===
